source_title: Costco Wholesale Corporation - Form 10-K (Fiscal Year Ended September 1, 2019)
publisher_issuer: Costco Wholesale Corporation (filed with U.S. SEC, EDGAR CIK 0000909832, accession 0000909832-19-000019)
company_context: Costco operates a membership-warehouse model in which the bulk of operating profit is effectively underwritten by recurring membership fees rather than merchandise margin. Sustained high renewal rates and steady comparable-sales growth are the core indicators of the model's durable health. Fiscal 2019 (year ended September 1, 2019) showed both at record levels.
geography: United States and international (headquartered United States)
macro_context: Strong consumer spending environment; e-commerce competition from Amazon and Walmart; warehouse-club category resilience driven by value perception and membership loyalty.
evidence_summary: Costco demonstrated sustained, stable health through membership loyalty rather than promotional churn. For fiscal 2019, net sales were $149.35 billion, up 7.9% from $138.43 billion the prior year. The membership renewal rate reached all-time highs: 90.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 88.4% worldwide (reported at the fourth-quarter / fiscal-year mark). The combination of high single-digit sales growth and record renewal demonstrates a durable, retention-driven model rather than a turnaround.
owner_decision_context: Management sustained its long-standing strategy of low merchandise markups, treating membership fees as the profit engine, and prioritized member value and renewal over short-term margin extraction, accepting thin product margins to protect loyalty.
action_taken: Maintained the high-renewal membership model: low prices, member value, disciplined SKU and warehouse operations, and steady unit growth, sustaining renewal and comparable performance year over year.
outcome_evidence: FY2019 net sales of $149.35B (+7.9%) alongside record renewal rates of 90.9% (U.S./Canada) and 88.4% (worldwide) confirm a stable, healthy, retention-driven business rather than one requiring intervention.
source_limitations: WebFetch of sec.gov typically returns HTTP 403 here; figures confirmed verbatim in WebSearch snippets attributed to Costco's FY2019 10-K and FY2019 results reporting. This record cites fiscal 2019 specifically and is distinct from any slice-1 Costco record citing a different fiscal year. The renewal rates are reported as of the fiscal-year/Q4 mark.
directly_stated: FY2019 net sales were $149.35 billion, up 7.9% from $138.43 billion the prior year
U.S. and Canada membership renewal rate was 90.9%, an all-time high
Worldwide membership renewal rate was 88.4%, an all-time high
inferred: Record renewal rates indicate negligible retention erosion and confirm the membership-fee profit engine is intact
Steady high-single-digit sales growth with rising renewal is best classified as stable-healthy, not a turnaround or shock
why_useful_for_opsiq: A baseline 'stable healthy' anchor where the key health signal is retention (renewal rate) rather than rescue. Useful as a hidden-key negative control: the engine should recognize a durable, well-run business and NOT prescribe intervention. Renewal rate is the load-bearing retention metric.
